claims.statement: Simpson's paradox can occur when a confounding variable (such as species in the Iris dataset) is overlooked, potentially leading to misleading or reversed conclusions about the association between two variables.

When analyzing the Iris dataset, distance-based or correlation-based methods may be sensitive to the scale and units of sepal length and petal length measurements, though both are typically measured in centimeters.
To obtain unconfounded estimates of the association between sepal length and petal length in the Iris dataset, species should be incorporated as a stratification or grouping variable in the analysis.
